revisions.title: A sudden wisdom descends
revisions.body: Socrates presents his sudden fluency with etymology as a daimonic wisdom attributed to Euthyphro. He proposes using it for today's inquiry, then purifying himself tomorrow by finding a priest or sophist able to expel it. The joke matters because the proposed purification targets the inspiration itself, not the inquiry it temporarily fuels.

revisions.title: Cratylus takes the handoff — and overreaches
revisions.body: After a brief challenge at 427e, Cratylus takes up the exchange at 428a. He holds that a wrong name is no name and that false speech is impossible. Socrates tests the position through images: a portrait may resemble well or badly, so naming, too, can admit degrees of correctness.
